entries.title: Amos 6:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: At ease - That neither fear nor believe the threatened judgments of God. In Zion - That is put for the kingdom of the two tribes, and principally the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Samaria - Woe to them also who rely upon the strength, wealth, and policy of the kingdom of Samaria or Israel. Which - Which two cities, Zion and Samaria. Named chief - Accounted the chief cities of that part of the world. To whom - To which place all Israel had recourse, the two tribes to Zion, the ten tribes to Samaria.

entries.title: Amos 6:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pass ye - Run over the history of that great and ancient city. Hemath - Head of the Syrian kingdom, lately overthrown by Tiglath - Pilneser, and a fresh instance of God's just indignation against secure sinners. Gath - The chief city of the Philistines, a few years before wasted by the arms of Hazael; by these examples learn to amend your ways, or expect to perish in them. Greater - That is, greater than these kingdoms of Israel and Judah, and their borders, or bounds, greater than these of Israel and Judah.

entries.title: Amos 6:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: That lie - That out of laziness or luxury, lay themselves to rest. And eat - The very best in all their flock.

entries.title: Amos 6:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: That chant - That in a time of deep mourning entertain themselves with songs, and musical instruments.

entries.title: Amos 6:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In bowls - Not in little vessels, but probably bowls: they drank these filled as full as they could hold too, and in design to drink each other down. And anoint - In those hot countries this anointing was much used. Not grieved - Nothing affected with the calamities of their country.

entries.title: Amos 6:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The banquet - The feastings of voluptuous ones shall cease.

entries.title: Amos 6:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The excellency - All that the seed of Jacob accounts a glory and excellency to them, all their external privileges and worship.

entries.title: Amos 6:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Remain - Escaping the enemies sword. Ten men - Many men, a certain number for an uncertain. They shall die - Tho' they escape a while, they shall not finally escape.

entries.title: Amos 6:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Uncle - Or near kinsman, instead of those who were wont to do this, and were paid for it; but now none of these remaining, the next to the dead must, as well as he is able, take him up on his shoulders, and carry him. That burneth - Though the Jews mostly buried, yet in some cases they burned the dead bodies, as in this of pestilence. The bones - The flesh being consumed, the bones are reserved to be buried. Unto him - Any one he sees near the house out of which the bones are carried. Is there yet any - Is any one living in your house. Hold thy tongue - Do not complain, lest thou thyself be killed, lest all be rifled. For - It is too late to seek God, who is executing his immutable decree.

entries.title: Amos 6:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For behold - It seems to be the continued speech of him who took care of the dead, ver. 10, God hath sent out war, famine, and pestilence. The great house - The palaces of great men shall have great breaches made in them, and the cottages of poor men shall, by lesser strokes, be ruined.

entries.title: Amos 6:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shall horses - If prophets exhort or advise, it does no more good than if you would run your horses upon the precipices of rocks.

entries.title: Amos 6:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Who rejoice - In your victories, alliances, and idols. Have we not - We have raised ourselves to greatness by our wisdom and courage.

entries.title: Amos 6:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hemath - A city of Syria, bordering on Israel, north - east. The wilderness - Which is the south - west parts of Canaan. So all your country shall be destroyed.
